CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ankle injury sustained during basketball.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
45-year-old male presents after a basketball injury at the court with his son. Patient went up for a shot and was contacted by his son while airborne. Upon landing, patient rolled and twisted his right ankle. Patient reports pain on the outside of the ankle with visible bruising and swelling. Patient endorses difficulty walking and reports the ankle does not feel stable. Patient recently returned to a regular gym routine and is concerned about interrupting his workout progress. Patient also volunteers to coach basketball starting in April.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient plays basketball recreationally with his 10-year-old son. Patient works from home. Patient has dogs. Patient has recently returned to regular exercise and gym routine.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not discussed.
General: Alert, cooperative 45-year-old male.
Right ankle: Swelling on the lateral side. Exquisite tenderness laterally. Some tenderness over medial deltoid region. Skin intact. Brisk capillary refill. No malalignment. Patient able to stand on ankle but reports pain with ambulation and subjective instability.

RESULTS
X-ray of right ankle (AP, lateral, and oblique views): Displaced lateral malleolus fracture at Weber C level. No evidence of medial or posterior malleolar fractures. Fracture noted to be in an unstable position.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Lateral malleolus fracture, right ankle, Weber C, displaced and unstable.
Plan: Surgical intervention with open reduction and internal fixation using plate and screws. Patient prescribed meloxicam for swelling. Ice ankle and keep elevated. Provide crutches. Patient counseled that recovery will take approximately three months. Patient may continue coaching in April but will need to limit weight-bearing activities during recovery. Follow-up to be arranged to monitor progress and initiate rehabilitation.
